name: KAWF Promotional Championship
epitaph: The federation's own second-tier singles prize, described in its own recruitment document as the one fans see most often; crowned vacant on the 2004 comeback broadcast.
notes: The federation's own recruitment document (8 April 2004) describes it as defended at least every 30 days and, on overseas tours, every other show.

name: KAWF Streetlife Championship
epitaph: The federation's own hardcore prize -- no-disqualification, falls count anywhere -- changing hands in a ladder-and-tables tag match on the 2004 comeback broadcast.
notes: The federation's own recruitment document (8 April 2004) describes it as defended at least every 30 days.

name: KAWF Global Championship
epitaph: The federation's own original top championship; vacant entering its 2004 comeback season and left unresolved after interference ended a grudge match for it on the comeback broadcast. Discontinued by the time of the federation's own 2006 second comeback, whose own recruitment document states plainly: "Were not going Global this time around so that title was axed."
notes: The federation's own recruitment document (8 April 2004) calls it the heavyweight championship, defended at least every two months; a news bulletin the same week as the comeback broadcast lists the title vacant.

name: KAWF Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The federation's own tag-team prize, left vacant entering the 2004 comeback season and decided in a four-way elimination match at the federation's own first pay-per-view.
notes: Attested as vacant from the federation's own earliest 2004 news bulletins onward; the four teams that filled its own inaugural four-way match were Youth Gone Wrong, the Boys Next Door, the Natural Criminals and the True All Stars.

name: KAWF Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: A new lightweight championship the federation introduced after its own first pay-per-view, decided in a bracketed tournament won by Sammy Griffin on Fever in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, 7 August 2004.
notes: The federation's own news bulletins name the tournament's first-round pairings (Sammy Griffin vs. Colt Montana, Tommy Flames vs. Peter Hilo, "Playboy" Tyler Rose vs. DJ Hawthorne, Ceaser Risley vs. Shadow of Style); no card transcript for the tournament final survives in this collection's own holdings, but KAWF Update #17 (6 December 2004) confirms Sammy Griffin as champion, crowned on Fever in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, 7 August 2004.

name: KAWF Women's Championship
epitaph: The federation's own first women's championship, introduced for its 2006 second comeback and decided in a triple-threat match at the promotion's own December supercard.
notes: The federation's own first-ever women's match, a non-title bout between Josie Saito and Nikki Glass, was held at 'Welcome Home' (30 September 2006) three months before this title was contested.

name: KAWF Mason Dixon Championship
epitaph: A new championship introduced for the federation's own December 2006 supercard, decided in a four-man tournament.
